The chart reference used by the development pilot is an AI visual comparison to the historical chart and remains qualitative rather than expert gold.

novelty.judgment: OCR and chart digitization have extensive prior work; a failure diagnosis can still be a useful negative technical report. The bounded search did not establish novelty of the specific failure modes.

This package confirms the manifest count and saved summaries, without rerunning every hash or establishing independence of the verifier authors. These tools support source/version preservation and audit navigation.

novelty.judgment: Hash manifests and research-data verification are established practices. The package may serve as an applied case study; no claim to a new provenance method is supported.

candidates.audience: Researchers repeating access work for hard-to-find excavation records and plates
candidates.established: Saved logs document failed downloads and source-recovery routes; no normalized project-wide failure count is claimed. candidates.title: Reference-model selection and identifiability in generated administrative records
candidates.field: Computational archaeology; record linkage; latent-variable methods
candidates.audience: Researchers mapping symbols to known record systems and testing model selection
candidates.established: In generated systems, a fresh reference-only selector recovers 309/384 maps, compared with 283 for a fixed graph profile and 168 for slot-only mapping. candidates.title: Grouped prediction and restoration controls for short Indus records
candidates.field: Computational epigraphy; computational linguistics; statistical archaeology
candidates.audience: Researchers comparing predictive structure in short, duplicated archaeological records
candidates.established: The preserved unique-text evaluation reports a 0.84836-bit gain per noninitial sign under the alias-preserving split. The one-known-slot restoration evaluation reaches 33.81% exact top-one on 8,009 masks, and the matched unknown-gap estimator scores 46.30% against 51.07% for always predicting one. The gain is a measure of predictive structure and does not identify a language or meaning.
evidence_fields: nested_results.json: exact gain field retained in the contribution assessment
benchmark.json: mask count and top-one accuracy

novelty.judgment: The October 6 live precedent assessment found Yadav et al. 2010's deduplicated held-out restoration, plus other Indus restoration and non-specificity results. Object/alias grouping and the joint accuracy/loss tradeoff are narrower candidate contributions; publication priority is plausible but not a general first restoration claim.
novelty.precedent_search: Checked in the October 6 assessment; a broader search is needed before submission

candidates.missing_validation: Independent reproduction, reviewed source transcription, comparison to a faithful published baseline, and a genuinely fresh expert-annotated evaluation block.
candidates.smallest_form: Conference research paper with grouped prediction controls and a retained negative gap comparison
venues: International Conference on Natural Language Processing for the Digital Humanities (NLP4DH): research paper; confirm the next call's format
candidates.remaining_work: One to two weeks for related-work correction and a reviewer-ready reproduction package; fresh annotation would take longer.
provenance_notes: This registry bundle includes frozen, failed, synthetic, exploratory and superseded endpoints; legacy labels are retained per entry. The 46.30% gap-count score is the design-matched endpoint, not the earlier unmatched 43.05% score. The failed comparison remains beside the 51.07% constant-one baseline.

candidates.title: CISI Volume 1 scan duplication and counting conventions
candidates.field: Digital archaeology; library digitization
candidates.audience: Digital archaeology; library digitization researchers and data curators
candidates.established: The IGNCA-hosted CISI1 PDF has 862 pages. All embedded page-image lists on pages 1–431 equal those on pages 432–862: 431 duplicate groups at offset 431. Printed p.375 also carries catalogue corrigenda, including deletion of H266–H275 and relabelling H356A/B/C as H354A/B/C bis. Those printed corrigenda are prior editorial corrections; the project contribution is the scan-identity audit and explicit counting-unit notes.

candidates.title: Version joins and source-plate compatibility across derivative catalogues
candidates.field: Digital epigraphy; archaeological data quality
candidates.audience: Digital epigraphy; archaeological data quality researchers and data curators
candidates.established: Among 2,375 older-export rows carrying a CISI reference, 2,374 find a Lipi object, 2,243 match some face exactly and 2,293 after eroded 000 is ignored. All 179 Mayig objects find a Lipi identity. A qualitative AI plate audit finds 17 compatible and seven discrepant objects among 24 source-complete cases. The earlier export and Lipi share a maintainer: their agreement measures version stability. Any-face matches leave side identity unresolved; the plate judgments need expert review.

novelty.judgment: Exact-result publication priority has not been checked; useful source-audit evidence is retained.
novelty.precedent_search: Not done for the exact result

candidates.title: Completed October 2 dataset and rights landscape
candidates.field: Digital archaeology; data stewardship
candidates.audience: Digital archaeology; data stewardship researchers and data curators
candidates.established: The completed October 2 comparison covers 18 resources and reports 39 passing local count/missingness checks. Its historical CAA 2023 ICIT witness gives 4,665 objects, 5,650 texts, 17,966 legible sign occurrences and 16,015 images. These are dated source counts; no current census or new integrated corpus is established. The source comparison distinguishes reuse rights and count denominators, and proposes a 200-object pilot.

novelty.judgment: ICIT, CISI and the Helsinki editions are established predecessors. The contribution is a dated resource/rights comparison; no claim that an integrated corpus is absent or that the local collection is superior is supported.
